label: Beryllium oxide ceramic
summary: Some magnetrons and older high-power RF transistors use a beryllium oxide (beryllia) ceramic insulator. Whole, it is harmless. Broken, ground, cut or filed, its dust can cause chronic beryllium disease, an incurable lung illness.
signs: Pink, white or cream ceramic washer or block between the magnetron body and its terminals or antenna dome
Labelled BeO or marked with a warning on the part or in its datasheet
You can’t tell beryllia from ordinary alumina by eye: treat every magnetron ceramic as beryllia
do: Keep the magnetron whole, or remove its magnets by unbolting the outer frame without breaking ceramics
Store damaged magnetrons sealed in a bag
Work outdoors and wet any dust if a ceramic is already cracked
dont: Never crush, cut, drill, file or sand a magnetron’s ceramics
Never sweep or blow dust from a broken one
ppe: A P100 or FFP3 respirator and gloves if you must handle a broken ceramic
firstAid: There is no field treatment for inhaled beryllium dust: leave the area and avoid further exposure
Shortness of breath, a persistent cough, tiredness or weight loss, weeks or even years later, needs a doctor; tell them about beryllium
Cut by broken ceramic: wash it out well under running water; a cut that won't heal or a lump that forms there needs a doctor
